wrong: I have 30 years.
right: I am 30 years old.
why: English uses 'be' with age, not 'have'.
why_bg: На английски възрастта е с глагола „съм“, не с „имам“.

wrong: I am agree with you.
right: I agree with you.
why: 'Agree' is a verb on its own. No 'am' in front of it.
why_bg: „Agree“ си е глагол. Не се слага „am“ пред него.

wrong: I feel myself good today.
right: I feel good today.
why: 'Feel' doesn't take 'myself' in English.
why_bg: „Чувствам се“ на английски е само „I feel“, без „myself“.

wrong: How do you call this in English?
right: What do you call this in English?
why: The question word is 'what', not 'how'.
why_bg: Въпросът е с „what“, не с „how“, макар че на български казваме „как“.

wrong: What means this word?
right: What does this word mean?
why: Questions in the present simple need 'do' or 'does'.
why_bg: Въпросите в сегашно просто време искат „do/does“.

wrong: How it looks?
right: How does it look?
why: Same rule: add 'does' and keep the verb in the base form.
why_bg: Същото правило: „does“ плюс глагол в основна форма.

wrong: Can you say me the price?
right: Can you tell me the price?
why: 'Tell' takes a person directly. 'Say' does not.

wrong: He said me that he was late.
right: He told me that he was late.
why: Say something, but tell someone something.
why_bg: Казваш нещо (say something), но казваш на някого (tell someone).

wrong: I will explain you the process.
right: I will explain the process to you.
why: 'Explain' needs 'to' before the person.

wrong: Let's discuss about the budget.
right: Let's discuss the budget.
why: 'Discuss' takes no preposition.

wrong: It depends of the client.
right: It depends on the client.
why: Always 'depend on'.

wrong: She is married with a doctor.
right: She is married to a doctor.
why: 'Married to', not 'with'.

wrong: Please answer to my question.
right: Please answer my question.
why: 'Answer' takes no 'to' before the thing.

wrong: He entered in the room.
right: He entered the room.
why: 'Enter' needs no preposition.

wrong: I saw it on the picture.
right: I saw it in the picture.
why: Things are 'in' a picture or photo.
why_bg: На снимка е „in the picture“, не „on“.

wrong: I go to work with the bus.
right: I go to work by bus.
why: Transport takes 'by', with no article.
why_bg: Транспортът върви с „by“ и без член.

wrong: The meeting is in Monday.
right: The meeting is on Monday.
why: Days take 'on'.

wrong: I'll send it in the end of the week.
right: I'll send it at the end of the week.
why: 'At the end of' for time, 'in the end' means finally.
why_bg: „At the end of“ за момент, а „in the end“ значи накрая, в крайна сметка.

wrong: I have a question to you.
right: I have a question for you.
why: A question is 'for' someone.

wrong: Send me the report until Friday.
right: Send me the report by Friday.
why: 'By' means not later than. 'Until' means continuously up to.
why_bg: „By“ значи най-късно до. „Until“ значи през цялото време до.

wrong: I look forward to hear from you.
right: I look forward to hearing from you.
why: 'To' here is a preposition, so the verb takes -ing.
why_bg: Тук „to“ е предлог, затова глаголът е с -ing.

wrong: I am interesting in this course.
right: I am interested in this course.
why: You are interested; the course is interesting.

wrong: The meeting was very boring, so I was boring.
right: The meeting was boring, so I was bored.
why: -ing describes the thing, -ed describes the person.
why_bg: Формата с -ing описва нещото, а с -ed описва човека.

wrong: The party was very funny.
right: The party was great fun.
why: 'Funny' means it made you laugh. 'Fun' means enjoyable.
why_bg: „Funny“ значи смешно. За приятно се казва „fun“.

wrong: What is the actual situation?
right: What is the current situation?
why: English 'actual' means real, not current.

wrong: She is a very sympathetic colleague.
right: She is a very likeable colleague.
why: 'Sympathetic' means understanding of suffering, not nice.

wrong: Eventually we will need a second office.
right: Possibly we will need a second office.
why: 'Eventually' means in the end, not perhaps.

wrong: Please control the numbers before sending.
right: Please check the numbers before sending.
why: 'Control' means to have power over something.

wrong: We realized the project in six months.
right: We completed the project in six months.
why: 'Realize' means to understand something suddenly.

wrong: Our main concurrent lowered prices.
right: Our main competitor lowered prices.
why: 'Concurrent' means happening at the same time.

wrong: They pretend that the invoice was paid.
right: They claim that the invoice was paid.
why: 'Pretend' means to act falsely.

wrong: My brutal salary is 3,000 euro.
right: My gross salary is 3,000 euro.
why: Before deductions is 'gross'; after is 'net'.

wrong: I need more informations.
right: I need more information.
why: 'Information' is uncountable and has no plural.
why_bg: „Information“ е неброимо и няма множествено число.

wrong: Thank you for your advices.
right: Thank you for your advice.
why: 'Advice' is uncountable. For one item say 'a piece of advice'.
why_bg: „Advice“ е неброимо. За едно нещо: „a piece of advice“.

wrong: The news are very good.
right: The news is very good.
why: 'News' looks plural but takes a singular verb.
why_bg: „News“ изглежда множествено, но глаголът е в единствено число.

wrong: The police is investigating.
right: The police are investigating.
why: 'Police' always takes a plural verb.
why_bg: „Police“ винаги върви с глагол в множествено число.

wrong: We bought new furnitures for the office.
right: We bought new furniture for the office.
why: 'Furniture' is uncountable.

wrong: I have a big experience in sales.
right: I have a lot of experience in sales.
why: Uncountable 'experience' takes 'a lot of', not 'a big'.
why_bg: Неброимото „experience“ иска „a lot of“, не „a big“.

wrong: I work here since five years.
right: I have worked here for five years.
why: 'For' with a length of time, and the present perfect.
why_bg: „For“ за продължителност, плюс сегашно перфектно време.

wrong: I am working here since 2020.
right: I have been working here since 2020.
why: 'Since' with a starting point needs the present perfect.
why_bg: „Since“ с начална точка иска сегашно перфектно.

wrong: I have been to London last year.
right: I went to London last year.
why: A finished time needs the past simple.
why_bg: Приключил момент в миналото иска минало просто време.

wrong: I didn't went to the meeting.
right: I didn't go to the meeting.
why: After 'didn't', the verb stays in the base form.
why_bg: След „didn't“ глаголът остава в основна форма.

wrong: I will call you when I will arrive.
right: I will call you when I arrive.
why: After 'when', use the present, not 'will'.
why_bg: След „when“ се ползва сегашно време, не „will“.

wrong: If I will have time, I will help.
right: If I have time, I will help.
why: No 'will' after 'if' in this kind of sentence.
why_bg: След „if“ в този тип изречение не се слага „will“.

wrong: I send you the file yesterday.
right: I sent you the file yesterday.
why: 'Yesterday' needs the past form.

wrong: This solution is more better.
right: This solution is better.
why: 'Better' is already comparative.
why_bg: „Better“ вече е сравнителна степен, не се удвоява.

wrong: It was the most best result.
right: It was the best result.
why: 'Best' is already the superlative.

wrong: The report is very much interesting.
right: The report is very interesting.
why: 'Very much' doesn't go before an adjective.

wrong: The price is very big.
right: The price is very high.
why: Prices are high or low, not big or small.

wrong: There was a strong rain yesterday.
right: There was heavy rain yesterday.
why: Rain is heavy, not strong.

wrong: I did a mistake in the invoice.
right: I made a mistake in the invoice.
why: You make mistakes, you don't do them.

wrong: She makes her homework every evening.
right: She does her homework every evening.
why: Homework goes with 'do'.

wrong: Can you make a photo of the whiteboard?
right: Can you take a photo of the whiteboard?
why: Photos are taken.

wrong: I will make an exam in June.
right: I will take an exam in June.
why: Exams are taken.

wrong: We make business with three countries.
right: We do business with three countries.
why: 'Do business' is the fixed phrase.

wrong: Please close the light when you leave.
right: Please turn off the light when you leave.
why: Lights are turned on and off.
why_bg: Лампите се „turn on/off“, не се отварят и затварят.

wrong: They will make a party on Friday.
right: They will have a party on Friday.
why: You have or throw a party.

wrong: I must to finish this today.
right: I must finish this today.
why: 'Must' is followed by the bare verb, with no 'to'.

wrong: I look forward for your answer.
right: I look forward to your answer.
why: The phrase is 'look forward to'.

wrong: Everybody are ready for the call.
right: Everybody is ready for the call.
why: 'Everybody' takes a singular verb.
why_bg: „Everybody“ върви с глагол в единствено число.

wrong: Our team are working on it.
right: Our team is working on it.
why: In American and most business English, 'team' is singular.
why_bg: В бизнес английския „team“ обикновено е в единствено число.

wrong: I am in the bus, I will call you later.
right: I am on the bus, I will call you later.
why: You travel 'on' a bus, train or plane.
why_bg: В автобус, влак или самолет е „on“, не „in“.

wrong: Thanks God it is Friday.
right: Thank God it is Friday.
why: The fixed expression has no 's'.

wrong: I am with a car today.
right: I have my car with me today.
why: English doesn't use 'be with' for owning or bringing.
why_bg: На английски не се казва „съм с кола“ по този начин.

wrong: Till now we have three applications.
right: So far we have three applications.
why: 'So far' is the natural phrase for progress until now.
why_bg: За напредък досега естественият израз е „so far“.
